claims.text: Machine-learning potentials can accurately determine melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning potentials can accurately determine enthalpies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning potentials can accurately determine entropies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning potentials can accurately determine volume changes at melting in high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning potentials can accurately determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning potentials can determine these properties efficiently across the high-entropy-alloy family.
The proposed machine-learning potentials are trained using ab initio calculations or molecular-dynamics simulations.
Atomic arrangements and bonding mediate the thermodynamic behavior of high-entropy alloys at high temperatures and phase transitions.
Machine-learning potentials learn relationships between atomic arrangements and thermodynamic properties.
Learning relationships between atomic arrangements and thermodynamic properties enables accurate thermodynamic predictions.
The predicted melting-temperature MAE will be less than 50 K relative to experimental literature values.
The predicted enthalpy-of-fusion MAE will be less than 10% relative to experimental values.
The predicted entropy-of-fusion MAE will be less than 10% relative to experimental values.
The proposed approach applies to high-entropy alloys containing three to six principal elements.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims applicability across the high-entropy-alloy family, whereas the stated boundary restricts applicability to alloys with three to six principal elements and the uncertainty field explicitly questions applicability beyond six elements.
